t: Liangzhu was a highly stratified rice-farming society of the Yangtze River Delta whose jade, silk, ivory and lacquer went only to elite graves, a division that marks it as an early state.
Its centre, Liangzhu Ancient City near Hangzhou, enclosed 290 hectares with clay walls and six gates around a palace complex, with dams to the north, and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Its jade cong and bi set the standard for ritual jades across Neolithic China, and the culture vanished from the Taihu Lake area after about 2300 BCE, probably because of floods.
dyk: Liangzhu craftsmen used diamond tools to polish corundum axes to a mirror-like lustre, the earliest known use of diamond tools anywhere, and Liangzhu is the only prehistoric culture known to have worked sapphire.
ev: The Liangzhu culture emerges in the Yangtze River Delta
The culture disappears from the Taihu Lake area, probably after decades of heavy rain and flooding
Shi Xingeng first excavates the type site at Liangzhu in Yuhang County, Zhejiang
The Zhejiang provincial government announces the discovery of the base of the ancient city walls, the centre of the culture
The new Liangzhu Culture Museum is completed and opens
The archaeological ruins of Liangzhu City are inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site

f.homeland: The Yangtze River Delta and the Taihu Lake area of eastern China, centred on Zhejiang. Key sites: Liangzhu Ancient City and its Mojiaoshan palace complex in Yuhang, Hangzhou; the Yaoshan altar; Maqiao, Xindili, Miaoqian and Guangfulin.
f.period: c. 3300–2300 BCE; it flourished around 2500 BCE and disappeared from the Taihu Lake area after about 2300 BCE.
f.known: jade cong cylinders, bi discs and yue axes; the walled Liangzhu Ancient City; flood-control dams; paddy rice, irrigation and aquaculture; houses on stilts; corundum axes worked with diamond tools; black “eggshell” pottery; the Yaoshan altar
f.sources: Excavations since 1936, including the city wall bases announced in 2007; graded burials and grave goods; analysis of jade, tools and pottery; flood layers and climate records; ancient DNA from Maqiao and Xindili and a 2025 autosomal study.
